nw-l10-o1.note: Category B: assessed, but by activities rather than by an exam item, so the trace could not see it. The ROT13 station and the code-breaker challenge are where a pupil works a simple key. No exam item asks for a Caesar shift and none should: OCR examines why encryption is needed and how public and private keys differ, not the mechanics of a Roman cipher. The cipher is here to make the idea of a key concrete.

nw-l10-o2.note: Category B. x3 asks why the Wi-Fi key itself is never sent between the device and the access point, which is the handshake, in the words a question would use rather than the words of the outcome. The ordering activity on s5 is where it is practised.
